authority: AGENTS.md section 7: SAFETY_DISCHARGED requires that no safe caller can cause UB and that every remaining unsafe operation has an explicit validity contract; SAFE_COMPATIBLE requires the whole dependency closure discharged
AGENTS.md section 8: compatibility, safety and cryptography are separate evidence axes
AGENTS.md section 22: evidence is bound to a frozen candidate and a dependent measurement must be re-derived, not carried
one_sentence: The consumer closure's reachable set is not a conservative over-approximation: when a site loses resolution its admitted target set can shrink, so reachability can be lost without any code-level edge being removed, and the same bound is the oracle that justifies every negative exclusion.

candidates.source_delta: 74 insertions / 21 deletions in src/evp/skeymgmt.rs and src/provider/skeymgmt.rs (authority-parity fix), plus tests, court tools, court artefacts and the rebuilt install tree

measurements.consumer_invariance: The ssh consumer's .text, .data and .data.rel.ro are byte-identical between v1n and v1p; only .note.gnu.build-id (18 bytes) and .debug_line_str (2 bytes, the build directory name) differ. The reachability movement therefore cannot be caused by the consumer binary.
measurements.layout_movement: libcrypto .text 4,970,942 -> 4,951,534 bytes; 20 function symbols change size (DES_set_key -4,381, DES_set_key_checked -4,381, DES_random_key -4,334, DES_is_weak_key -4,320, digest_to_nid::ossl_digest_get_approved_nid -708, ENGINE_register_all_complete -561, rsa_item_sign -449). The DES sizes are explained by LLVM inlining DES_is_weak_key into its callers in v1n and not in v1p; DES_set_key_unchecked is unchanged and all five symbols keep distinct addresses. This is semantically neutral codegen variance from thin-local-LTO/codegen-unit partitioning, not a semantic change.
measurements.reproducibility: Each source tree is byte-reproducible in isolation (three builds each, including a fresh container and a touch-all cold recompile). The difference between v1n and v1p is source-induced at the build level and deterministic per tree.
measurements.analysis_identity: A comment-only edit to src/evp/skeymgmt.rs yields a different libcrypto digest (af568abe...) with byte-identical .text, identical section sizes, identical function sizes and identical symbol addresses (only .llvm.<hash> name suffixes differ). Therefore the DSO digest is not an identity for the analysis input; the analysis identity must be canonicalised over .text and the symbol table.

cbc_sites.got_slot_references: 25 call/jump instructions from 21 enclosing functions, identical sets in both DSOs (aes_cbc_cipher, provider::cipher::aes_cbc_run, camellia_cbc_run, ossl_cipher_hw_chunked_cbc, ossl_cipher_hw_generic_cbc, e_seed/e_aria/e_camellia/e_sm4 cbc ciphers, CRYPTO_cts128_encrypt_block, CRYPTO_nistcts128_encrypt_block, AES_cbc_encrypt, SEED_cbc_encrypt, Camellia_cbc_encrypt, ...)

lost_edge.v1n: site 0x5f4f7a in core::fmt::Formatter::pad, `jmp *%rax`, PROVED_TARGET_SET with 2 targets {CRYPTO_cbc128_encrypt, std::panicking::panic_count::finished_panic_hook}
lost_edge.v1p: site 0x5effaa, same instruction at the same position, UNRESOLVED, no targets
lost_edge.classification: resolver target-set classification changed for a site whose code did not change; not a removed call edge, not a caller becoming unreachable, not ICF aliasing
lost_edge.note: The v1n admission is itself implausible as a real call: a Formatter::pad tail jump cannot legitimately target a CBC block function. The bound is therefore noisy in both directions, not merely narrowing.

cbc_sites.v1p_status: The edge records are still emitted for every site of every closed DSO (52,033 records); the two CRYPTO_cbc128_encrypt records remain UNRESOLVED with missing_property reg-value-partial[int]. What changed is that the closure no longer counts the function as reachable, so the sites left reachable_residual_sites and the element-7 target-bounded count fell from 2 to 1. The disappearance is not silent at the record level, but it is unexplained at the graph level.

root_cause.statement: The unresolved-site admission is a class-specific set (taken_code, field-store values in start_set, unknown-call-argument targets in start_set) rather than a superset of everything the resolver may have admitted. A site that becomes less precise can therefore admit strictly fewer targets.
root_cause.evidence: Across the two sidecars, matching records by (normalised function, role, operand shape): 50,986 PROVED->PROVED, 771 UNRESOLVED->UNRESOLVED, 74 UNRESOLVED->PROVED, 59 PROVED->UNRESOLVED. The 59 losses drop whole evaluated unions (923 -> 0, 912 -> 0, ...). 3,462 sites show target churn. The largest movers are BIO_puts, BIO_ctrl, ASN1_sign and ec::mult ossl_ec_wNAF_pre, each losing a ~923-target union.

file_losses.note: 121 symbols present in both DSOs under identical names; no target set names any of them. The reachable function set is not persisted, so the lost direct edge cannot be named from the receipt.

root_cause.is_codegen: The DSO layout change is codegen (inlining/partitioning). The reachability loss is not entailed by codegen alone; it is the non-monotone bound interacting with resolver classification.

why_it_blocks: A dependency closure is only meaningful if the reachable set is an over-approximation. If reachability can be lost while the consumer is byte-identical, then 'not reachable' is not established, and the closure is not a proof of what the consumer can execute.

The same set is the negative-claim oracle introduced in edge-record v1.4. Every exclusion justified by 'not in the final upper bound' inherits this defect: the oracle check is necessary but not sufficient until the bound is sound.

Obligation counts are not carriable across candidates: 155 -> 171 obligations, 77 -> 78 discharged, 60 -> 63 blocked, 18 -> 30 unknown, 13 -> 17 missing boundary receipts, with no semantic change in the moved files. A discharge computed at S cannot be carried to S' (AGENTS section 22), and here it cannot even be reproduced across two candidates of the same semantic source.

Provider-implemented cipher/MAC coverage is incidental: those implementations are reached only when an unrelated evidence-class union happens to include them, because ABI_CONTRACT_PROVIDER is contract-bounded with an unbounded target set. That is not a principled reachability route.
required_remedy: Make the bound monotone: an unresolved site must admit at least the union of every evidence class it could satisfy and every target the resolver considered at that site; a class-specific set may refine reporting precision but must be proved a superset of the resolved set before it may bound reachability.

Add an executable invariant over a pair of sidecars: for every site keyed semantically, unresolved_bound(site) must be a superset of proved_bound(site) and of the union of both candidates' admitted sets. A violation is a refusal.

Add a neutrality control to the freeze: build S, rebuild S, and rebuild S with a comment-only edit; require a canonical analysis identity (hash over .text bytes plus the symbol table) to be identical across all three, and record the DSO digests as non-identities.
Persist the reachable function set (canonical digest plus the set) in the receipt, so a movement can be adjudicated from the receipt rather than reconstructed from 1.3 GB sidecars.

Fix the STALE_HASH rule collision: the build record hashes the pristine source tree with sha256('openssl-rs/source-tree/v1\0' + path\0bytes\0) while the atlas and consumer_closure compare canonical-JSON [[relpath,size,sha256]]. Both are recorded under the same field name, so the check always fails when provenance is supplied. Emit the canonical value as source_root_hash and the domain-separated value as source_tree_domain_hash, and compare like with like.
Re-run the ssh and sshd closures at the repaired bound, and publish the reachable-file and obligation diff, before any obligation is adjudicated or carried.
state_of_the_record_level_hardening: Unaffected and still valid: 52,033 records, 0 record defects, 0 oracle violations, 0 unattributable admissions, and every exclusion carries a subject-bound, recomputable claim. The defect is in the graph the records are validated against, not in the record discipline.
non_claims: This finding does not claim that any particular unsafe operation was missed or that any Rust code is unsound; it claims that the reachability bound cannot currently support a safety-relevant dependency closure.
No dynamic trace exists for ssh in either run (observed_trace.available = false), so whether ssh executes CRYPTO_cbc128_encrypt is not established either way.
Byte reproducibility across toolchains, machines or images is not established; only within the pinned court image.
SAFE_COMPATIBLE remains 0/33. No obligation discharge from v1n or v1p is carried forward by this receipt.
